claims.text: SQUID magnetometry with magnetic-susceptibility measurements can detect the presence of ferromagnetic ground states.
The method applies to a low-temperature ferromagnetic material.
A small applied magnetic field can be used to probe the material.
The measurement should be performed below the material's Curie temperature.
Magnetic domains are the structural mediator of the response.
An applied magnetic field aligns magnetic moments in the material.
Ferromagnetic behavior will produce a significant increase in magnetic susceptibility relative to a diamagnetic material at the same temperature.
The increase in magnetization per unit applied field will be at least 10% relative to a diamagnetic baseline.
Temperature above the Curie temperature is outside the boundary in which the proposed ferromagnetic response is expected.
The magnitude of the susceptibility increase may depend on the material and experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 10% increase, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only below 5%, leaving results from 5% to under 10% inconsistent with the prediction but non-falsifying under the stated rule.
